problem:
Given that $I(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{3}\,\text{d}x,$ calculate ${I}^{′}(t)$ for $t\in R$ by differentiating under the integral sign.

${I}^{′}(t)=3{e}^{-t}(\,$
{{field-1}}$)$
worked_solution:
Suppose $f(x,t)$ is continuous on $R=[a,b]\times [c,d]$ and $\frac{∂f}{∂t}$ exists and is continuous on $R.$ Then, the function

$$
F(t)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x
$$

is differentiable on $(c,d),$ and

$$
{F}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{∂f}{∂t}(x,t)\,\text{d}x.
$$

This is known as *differentiating under the integral sign.*

We wish to compute ${I}^{′}(t),$ where

$$
I(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{3}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Differentiating under the integral sign, we get

$$
{I}^{′}(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{∂}{∂t}[({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{3}]\,\text{d}x.
$$

Next, let's compute the partial derivative with respect to $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂t}[({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{3}] & =3({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂t}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t}) \\  & =3({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{2}\cdot {e}^{-t} \\  & =3{e}^{-t}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this back into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}^{′}(t) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{e}^{-t}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{e}^{-t}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's evaluate the remaining integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{e}^{-t})^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-2{x}^{2}{e}^{-t}+{e}^{-2t})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}{|}_{0}^{1}-{e}^{-t}\cdot \frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}{|}_{0}^{1}+{e}^{-2t}\cdot x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}-\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-t}+{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{I}^{′}(t)=3{e}^{-t}(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{2}{3}{e}^{-t}+{e}^{-2t}).
$$
